title: problem
description: What went wrong, in the one shape every app uses (ADR-S21): an error, when the request failed, in an answer's errors; or a problem the answer worked around, in its problems. A program decides by code and reason, never by message (G-STACK-15). A field that does not apply is left out, never null.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/contracts/problem/v1: names this schema wherever the Problem appears, so it can be read even on its own (ADR-S15).

kind.description: Always Problem, so a problem is told apart from every other kind, even outside an answer.

code.description: What happened, as an open word a program decides by; a reader matches the words it knows and shows the message for any other, so an app can report a new word without a new contract (CT-RULE-1). Known words: unread: a part was left out and the rest kept; refused: the whole thing was not taken; undeclared: it names something that is not declared; old: it is in an old form, which a migrate fixes; unsupported_contract: the asked contract version is not served, and supported lists the ones to ask again with (ADR-S03).

reason.description: Why it happened, when a program needs more than the code to decide; an open word, read like code. Left out when the code says enough. Known words: wrong_type: a value is of another type than the field takes; empty: a value that must say something is empty; unknown_key: a key the shape does not have; out_of_range: a value outside what the field allows; duplicate: another place already holds the same thing.

at.description: Where it happened: the first place is where it happened, any others what it clashes with, so a person or a tool goes straight to them. Left out when the problem is about no place.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain words for a person. A program reads code and reason instead, so this text may be reworded.

supported.description: For unsupported_contract only: the contract versions the app answers. A reader that asked for a version the app cannot give picks one from this list that it also speaks and asks again (ADR-S03, ADR-S06).

items.description: One contract version the app answers, such as v1.

place.description: One place a problem points to. Every field is optional, as a problem may know only the file, or only the field, but a place says at least one thing.

file.description: The file, as a path inside the folder the app works on, so the same problem reads the same on every machine; never a machine path, so it has no leading slash, no drive letter and no .. step.

document.description: Which document in that file or input, counted from 1, as one file may hold several.

line.description: The line where it starts in the real file, counted from 1, so an editor can jump there.

path.description: The field inside the document, as a path such as metadata.id, so a person finds the exact value to fix.
